# Which Way Is "Positive"?

<!-- STEP id="pick-a-direction" -->
Before plugging numbers into $v = u + at$, pick one direction to call positive — usually the direction the object starts out moving in. Everything else is measured against that choice.

<!-- STEP id="speeding-up-same-sign" -->
A car speeding up in that positive direction has velocity **and** acceleration both positive. They point the same way.

<!-- STEP id="slowing-down-opposite-sign" -->
A car braking — still moving in the positive direction, just slowing — has **negative** acceleration, even though it hasn't started going backwards.

Velocity and acceleration now point opposite ways.

<!-- STEP id="the-rule" -->
**Same sign as velocity → speeding up. Opposite sign → slowing down.** Get the sign of $a$ wrong, and every kinematic equation gives a wrong answer — even when the algebra is otherwise perfect.
